title: Yu Gong, the Foolish Old Man Who Moved the Mountains
theme: Taking on something so big it will outlast you, and keeping at it day after day anyway.
also: Robert the Bruce and the Spider

title: The Oak and the Reeds
theme: When pushing harder won’t work, and strength means bending, carrying, and letting yourself be guided.
also: The Annunciation: “Let it be with me”

title: Stone Soup
theme: A hard, hungry start where nobody trusts anyone yet, and the only way forward is to get others to join in.

title: The Full Cup
theme: Coming to learn something while already sure you know it, so nothing new can get in.

title: Jiang Ziya Fishes with a Straight Hook
theme: Waiting for a chance you can’t force, and staying calm, ready and true to yourself while it doesn’t come.
also: Juan Tamad and the Guava Tree

title: The Snipe and the Clam
theme: Being locked in a fight where neither side will let go, while someone else stands to gain.

title: Sun Tzu Drills the Palace Ladies
theme: Having to turn a loose group of people into a team that truly follows through, and owning the discipline that takes.

title: Alan Qo’a and the Five Arrows
theme: A family or group starting to drift apart, and the need to hold together before it is too late.

title: The North Wind and the Sun
theme: You want to move someone or something that will not budge, and pushing harder only makes them dig in.

title: The Tiger Keeper
theme: You have to live or work close to someone powerful and dangerous, and one careless step could cost you dearly.

title: The Long Spoons
theme: Everything you need is already on the table. Whether it feels like plenty depends on whether people reach toward each other.

title: The Sacred Tortoise in the Mud
theme: You are offered honour and position by a system you do not trust, and the price may be yourself.
also: Why the Sky Is Far Away

title: Ruth and Naomi
theme: A bond that is chosen rather than inherited, open to the outsider, and strong enough to carry people through loss.
also: Momotarō, the Peach Boy, and His Companions

title: Croesus and Solon
theme: Things are going very well for you, and the real question is how you hold what you have.

title: Hillel and the Wager
theme: Someone is trying to get a rise out of you, and real stature means not needing to prove anything.
also: Anansi and the Pot of Wisdom

title: The Bremen Town Musicians
theme: When you feel finished or unwanted, a spark of shared enthusiasm can gather others and get everyone moving again.

title: Three Visits to the Thatched Cottage
theme: Choosing whom to follow, and how a leader earns followers by first being willing to bow to real worth.

title: Yu the Great Tames the Flood
theme: Inheriting a mess that someone before you made, and setting it right without repeating their mistake.

title: Emperor Nintoku and the Kitchen Smoke
theme: A good season of growth, and the leader who comes close to people to look after them rather than to take from them.
also: Harun al-Rashid Walks the City at Night

title: The Blind Men and the Elephant
theme: Seeing only part of the picture and mistaking it for the whole, and the need to look wider before you judge.

title: Judge Bao and the Ox’s Tongue
theme: A lie or a wrong stuck in the middle of things that has to be bitten through with a clear, firm judgment.

title: Buying the Box and Returning the Pearl
theme: Being so taken with the packaging that you overlook what it was meant to hold.

title: Bian Que and Duke Huan of Cai
theme: A slow decline that starts small and quietly, and the cost of refusing to see it while it can still be stopped.

title: The Prodigal Son
theme: Turning back after you have gone astray, and being welcomed home sooner than you dared to hope.

title: The Old Man at the Frontier Loses His Horse
theme: Things happen to us that we did not plan or deserve. We are quick to call them good or bad before the story is over.

title: Joseph and the Seven Years of Plenty
theme: A season of plenty or strength is the time to store it up and train it. Then it is there when it is truly needed.

title: The Town Mouse and the Country Mouse
theme: What we feed on, and what we envy in other people’s plates, quietly shapes the life we end up living.

title: Noah Builds the Ark
theme: When a whole situation is about to give way, someone has to take bold, unusual steps, even if it means standing alone.

title: The Swimmer at Lüliang Falls
theme: When we are in danger again and again, fighting the current only drowns us. Staying true and moving with it carries us through.

title: Icarus
theme: Brightness and talent burn out when they forget what holds them up, and last when they keep to the middle way.

title: Bo Ya and Zhong Ziqi, the Friend Who Knew the Sound
theme: The deepest bond is not won by pressing or pleasing, but by two people who truly hear each other.
also: Malakas and Maganda, from the Split Bamboo

title: Philemon and Baucis
theme: What lasts, in a marriage or a life, is not something grand but a steady faithfulness renewed every ordinary day.

title: Fan Li Sails Away
theme: Walking away at the height of success, before a powerful situation turns against you.

title: The Two Goats on the Bridge
theme: Having plenty of strength and wanting to push, when the real test is whether to hold back.
also: Thor in the Hall of Utgard-Loki

title: Dick Whittington and His Cat
theme: Rising in the world, when your chance comes through generosity and a little help from others.
also: The Carp That Leapt the Dragon Gate

title: Han Xin Crawls Between the Butcher’s Legs
theme: Enduring humiliation in a dark time without giving away who you really are.

title: Mencius’s Mother Moves Three Times
theme: Shaping the people you love by what you do and where you put them, not by lectures.
also: The Old Grandfather and the Grandson

title: Lian Po Carries the Thorns
theme: Two people at odds, when one chooses not to fight because something larger is at stake.

title: Jonah
theme: Running from the thing you must face, and finding every road blocked until you turn back.

title: The Lion and the Mouse
theme: Letting someone off, or being freed yourself, and finding that release runs both ways.

title: Diogenes Throws Away His Cup
theme: Having less, by necessity or by choice, and finding that what remains is enough.

title: The Monkey King Who Became a Bridge
theme: A season of growth, when those who have more give of themselves and everyone ends up richer.

title: The Emperor’s New Clothes
theme: The moment when something everyone half knows has to be said out loud.
also: Nathan and David: “You Are the Man”

title: The Camel’s Nose in the Tent
theme: The small first step of something you should not let in, which looks harmless when it arrives.

title: The Conference of the Birds
theme: People coming together around something greater than any one of them, and what it costs to arrive.

title: Milo and the Calf
theme: Growing strong or great slowly, by adding a little every single day.
also: Ninomiya Sontoku Plants the Cast-off Seedlings

title: Kisa Gotami and the Mustard Seed
theme: Being at the end of your strength, when no one seems to hear you and the only way out is through.

title: The Gardener and the Well-Sweep
theme: The deep source people draw on, and why keeping it clear matters more than a cleverer bucket.

title: The Ugly Duckling
theme: Becoming who you really are takes a long, hard season, and the change shows only when its time has come.

title: Yi Yin, the Cook Who Became Minister
theme: Real worth can enter by the kitchen door, and the person who nourishes others well can end up shaping a whole order.

title: Henny Penny
theme: A sudden fright can send us running in all directions, unless we stop and look at what actually hit us.

title: The Wind and the Flag
theme: When everyone is arguing about what is moving out there, the stillness we need is inside.

title: The Man Who Pulled Up the Sprouts
theme: Some things grow only at their own pace, and the harder we pull, the more we kill them.

title: Wang Zhaojun Goes Beyond the Wall
theme: Entering a situation on someone else’s terms, with little say, you can still act with grace and change how it ends.

title: This Too Shall Pass
theme: At the very top of good fortune, the wisest thing is to shine fully and remember it will not last.

title: Chong’er and the Clod of Earth
theme: Far from home and without standing, how we take an insult decides whether we ever get home at all.

title: Cook Ding Carves the Ox
theme: When force has failed and what is needed is patient, attentive work that finds the natural way through.

title: Amaterasu and the Cave of Laughter
theme: When someone has withdrawn into gloom and no argument will bring them out, but shared, honest delight might.

title: The Burning of the Rice Fields
theme: When people are scattered or in danger, and the only thing that will gather them is a real sacrifice.

title: The Fisherman and His Wife
theme: When wanting more has no end, and someone cannot say where enough is.

title: The Man Who Loved the Seagulls
theme: When someone wants to win trust, or to use it, and finds that hidden intentions are felt before anything is said.

title: The Tortoise Who Talked Too Much
theme: When pride makes it hard to keep quiet, and one small retort could undo everything.

title: “Do Not Forget Ju”
theme: When things have finally come right, and the danger is forgetting how hard it was to get here.

title: Orpheus and Eurydice
theme: When the end is almost in reach and the hardest thing is to keep trusting for the last few steps.
also: One Basket Short of the Mountain
